subject: no-code-automation
question: Will the Invoices folder contain only supplier invoices?

artifact.workflow:
Trigger: New email in accounts@acme.example (Gmail)
Action: Upload each attachment to Drive folder 'Invoices'
Goal: keep a folder of supplier invoices.

ai_claim: Yes. Suppliers email their invoices to this inbox, so the attachments uploaded are the invoices.

ai_solution.text: The workflow runs on every new email.
So the folder contains the invoices.

failure.explanation: The workflow uploads every attachment from every email: signature logos, newsletters, spam, internal replies with screenshots, and duplicate invoices in reply threads. The folder fills with non-invoices, making it unusable. Add filters (sender domain allowlist, PDF only, subject contains 'invoice') and deduplicate.
failure.why_convincing: The inbox's main purpose is invoices, so its attachments seem to be invoices.

canonical_solution: No: every attachment is saved, including logos and spam. Filter by sender, file type and subject.

valid_evidence.summary: A week's run saved 214 files: 61 invoices, 98 signature images, 55 other attachments.
Workflows should validate and filter inputs before acting.

counterexamples: An email signature logo lands in the Invoices folder.

hints.text: Think about all the emails this inbox receives.
Step 3 uploads without checking.
Automations need filters that match their goal.
Count what one week's run saved.
Step 3 is wrong: every attachment is saved. Add filters.

repair: Add filters: sender domain allowlist, PDF attachments, subject keywords; dedupe by file hash.
debrief: An automation does exactly what it is told, at scale. Specify precisely which inputs it should act on.

subject: no-code-automation
question: Will every registrant get the SMS and will the workflow run cleanly?

artifact.workflow:
Trigger: New form submission (fields: name, email, phone - phone optional)
Action 1: Add row to CRM
Action 2: Send SMS 'Thanks for registering' to {{phone}}
AI: "Every registrant gets the SMS confirmation."

ai_claim: Yes. Every submission triggers the workflow, and the SMS step sends to the phone field, so every registrant gets it.

ai_solution.text: The SMS is sent to the phone number.

failure.misconception: Not handling an empty optional field
failure.explanation: Phone is optional. For registrants who leave it blank, the SMS step has no recipient: it errors (possibly halting or flagging the run) and those people get no confirmation. Add a filter or branch: send SMS only if phone is not empty, and email the others instead.
failure.why_convincing: Test submissions usually fill in every field.

canonical_solution: No: blank phone numbers make the SMS step fail. Branch on whether phone is present.

valid_evidence.summary: A submission without a phone number produces the error 'Recipient number is required' at Action 2.
submission (phone empty) -> CRM row added -> SMS step fails -> no confirmation sent

counterexamples: People who skip the phone field get no confirmation.

hints.text: Submit the form without a phone number.
Step 3 assumes phone is always present.
Workflows must handle optional and missing fields.
Look at what the SMS step receives.
Step 3 is wrong: empty phones break the SMS step. Add a branch.

repair: Add a condition: if phone is not empty, send SMS; otherwise send an email confirmation.
debrief: Test automations with minimal, not just complete, inputs.

subject: no-code-automation
question: Will the workflow keep sending confirmations after Priya's account is deactivated?

artifact.workflow:
The company's order-confirmation workflow sends emails through Priya's personal work Gmail connection, which she authorised when she built it.
Priya is leaving the company next week; her account will be deactivated.
AI: "The workflow belongs to the company workspace, so it will keep running after she leaves."

ai_claim: Yes. The workflow is stored in the company's workspace, so it keeps running regardless of who built it.

ai_solution.text: The workflow lives in the company workspace.
So it continues after Priya leaves.

failure.explanation: The workflow's email step authenticates with Priya's account. When it is deactivated, the connection's token becomes invalid and every run fails - order confirmations stop. Move connections to a shared service account (e.g. orders@), document owners, and review connections in the offboarding checklist.
failure.why_convincing: The workflow itself is visibly in the company's space.

canonical_solution: No: the email step uses Priya's credentials, which will stop working. Reconnect with a shared service account.

valid_evidence.summary: account deactivated -> OAuth token revoked -> 'invalid_grant' on every send -> confirmations stop
Production automations should use service accounts, not personal credentials.

counterexamples: The day after Priya leaves, confirmations stop.

hints.text: Check whose credentials the email step uses.
Step 3 assumes ownership of the workflow covers its connections.
Connections are authorised by individual accounts.
Deactivate the account in a test.
Step 3 is wrong: the connection depends on Priya's account. Use a service account.

repair: Reconnect with a shared service account and add connections to offboarding.
debrief: Automations inherit the lifecycle of the credentials they use. Personal credentials make business processes fragile.

subject: no-code-automation
question: Will the summary be posted at 9 AM India time?

artifact.workflow:
Trigger: Schedule - every day at 09:00
Account time zone setting: UTC (default, never changed)
Action: Post the daily sales summary to the team channel.
AI: "The summary will be posted at 9 AM for the Bengaluru team."

ai_claim: Yes. The schedule says 09:00, so the summary is posted at 9 AM for the team.

ai_solution.text: So it is posted at 9 AM.

failure.misconception: Ignoring the account's time zone setting
failure.explanation: Schedules run in the account's (or workflow's) time zone. With UTC, 09:00 is 14:30 IST - the summary arrives mid-afternoon. Set the account or workflow time zone to Asia/Kolkata, or schedule 03:30 UTC.

canonical_solution: No: 09:00 UTC is 14:30 IST. Set the time zone to Asia/Kolkata.

valid_evidence.summary: Scheduled triggers use the configured time zone.

counterexamples: The morning summary arrives at 2:30 PM.

hints.text: Check the account's time zone.
Step 3 assumes 09:00 means local time.
Schedules follow the configured time zone.
Convert 09:00 UTC to IST.
Step 3 is wrong: it runs at 14:30 IST. Fix the time zone.

repair: Set the workflow's time zone to Asia/Kolkata.
debrief: Every time in an automation has a time zone, stated or not. Check which one.

subject: no-code-automation
question: Is the AI right that this design avoids duplicate contacts?

artifact.workflow:
Trigger: New order in the shop
Step 1: Search CRM for a contact with this email
Step 2 (if found): Update the contact's last_order_date
Step 3 (if not found): Create a new contact
AI: "Repeat customers are updated, not duplicated, and re-running an order does not create duplicates."

ai_claim: Yes. The workflow looks for an existing contact by email first, updates it if found and creates one only if not, so repeat customers and re-runs do not create duplicates.

ai_solution.text: The CRM is searched by email before any change.
New contacts are created only when no match exists.
Re-running for the same order finds the contact and updates it again.

canonical_solution: Correct. Search-before-create (an upsert) keyed on a stable identifier makes the workflow idempotent for contacts. (Normalising email case helps matching.)

valid_evidence.summary: Two orders from asha@example.com produce one contact with the latest order date.

hints.text: Follow a repeat customer's second order.
Step 4 covers re-runs.
Upserts keyed on a unique field prevent duplicates.
Run the workflow twice for the same order.
This solution is correct. Search-before-create avoids duplicates. The right judgment was to approve it.

debrief: Design automations so running them twice is harmless. Upserts are the simplest way.
